title: Marketing Info Systems Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 7
description:
Every Friday, Laddoo Lab sells out by noon. Every Monday, packs come back unsold. The answers were there all along, in Arjun's sales notebook, Dev's customer messages and Nani's memory, but nobody put them together. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, to understand the marketing information system (MIS).

You will see Philip Kotler's idea of the firm's marketing nerve center (Business Horizons, 1966) and his textbook definition, then watch Laddoo Lab build its own system in five live steps: gather, sort, analyze, share and decide, until unsold packs fall from 20 a week to 4 (example figures). We break the system into Kotler's four parts, internal records, marketing intelligence, marketing research and decision support, and compare intelligence (always on, like a radar) with research (one question, like a torch). Then we see each part at work today, in a bakery, an airline, a phone maker and a food delivery app. We also look at the human side honestly: data cuts guesswork and waste, but too much or old data misleads, and customer data must be kept safe. In India, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 allows fines of up to Rs 250 crore for failing to protect personal data.

This is Episode 7 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
